question: In an office with 40 officers, the average salaries of class-A, class-B and class-C officers are ₹600, ₹750 and ₹1,000 a day, respectively. The numbers of class-A, class-B and class-C officers in the office are in the ratio 5 ∶ 4 ∶ 1, respectively. Find the monthly average salary (in ₹) of an officer, all the 40 of them taken together. [Assume the number of days in a month to be 30.]
solution:
**Given:**

In an office with 40 officers, the average salaries of class-A, class-B and class-C officers are ₹600, ₹750 and ₹1,000 a day, respectively.

The numbers of class-A, class-B and class-C officers in the office are in the ratio 5 ∶ 4 ∶ 1

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of elements/Number of elements

**Calculation:**

The numbers of class-A, class-B and class-C officers = 20, 16, 4

Now,

Salaries of class-A = 600 × 20 × 30

⇒ 600 × 600

⇒ 360000

Salaries of class-B = 750 × 16 × 30

⇒ 750 × 480

⇒ 360000

Salaries of class-C = 1000 × 4 × 30

⇒ 4000 × 30

⇒ 120000

Total = 360000 + 360000 + 120000

⇒ 840000

Average = 840000/40

⇒ 21000

**∴ The monthly average salary (in ₹) of an officer, all 40 of them taken together is 21,000.**
